title: बारह बजे
logline: At half past ten Bhaiyaji phones his 'Inspector साहब' and invites him to the godown at midnight, alone, to stamp the slip for eight hundred sacks of ration grain. Pushpa brings news that the SHO's call to Bhaiyaji connected that evening. The DSP refuses a raid, orders Nirala locked up now and says any officer who helps him will be named in the same FIR. Nirala lays a carved teak revolver on the desk and holds out his wrists, and Nandini has to choose.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.

characters.name: नंदिनी जोशी (Nandini Joshi)
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, six weeks into her first posting at the Imlipur thana. Tonight she is in the fake thana with its 'Inspector', with his files and with an order to have him in her lockup before ten tomorrow.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars. Her cherry-red open-face scooter helmet sits on the complainants' bench all episode.
characters.voice_note: Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Educated small-city north-Indian Hindi with crisp English police and office words; the most English-mixed speaker in the cast. Quick and clipped. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. Tonight she is under pressure from b6 on: every line after that is lower and more exact than the one before.

characters.name: सुधीर निराला (Sudhir Nirala)
characters.role: The self-appointed 'Inspector' of the fake thana in the shut Roopam Talkies. To Bhaiyaji he is 'Inspector साहब'; to Nandini and Pushpa, 'निराला जी'.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. A home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping past his shoulders, sleeves to his knuckles, collar standing away from his neck, trousers belted high with the belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge, worn dead level. One large home-made medal above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm on a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon. Brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip, holding the wooden revolver until b8.
characters.voice_note: Male, forty, light careful tenor. Small-town north-Indian Hindi in an official register, English police terms pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Under pressure he becomes more formal and quieter and his sentences get shorter. Frightened is a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. Tonight he is frightened from b1 on; play b8 and b9 straight, with no comic colour at all.

characters.name: पुष्पा कुमारी (Pushpa Kumari)
characters.role: Head Constable at the Imlipur thana for twenty-six years. She heard part of the SHO's call to Bhaiyaji at seven and has walked across the line to say so.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on each teal epaulette, lantern sleeve patches, under an open hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan with two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. A cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Small-town Hindi, plain and economical; says the important thing in the fewest words. Never surprised. Tonight she arrives out of breath from the walk, but the facts come out level and exact.

characters.name: बलराम 'भैयाजी' ठाकुर (Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur)
characters.role: Runs the ration godown and most of Imlipur. Voice only in this episode, on Nirala's keypad phone, on speaker.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Small-town north-Indian Hindi, courteous to the point of menace; never threatens, never hurries, laughs before he says the worst thing. Tonight he sounds ordinary and friendly: the invitation must sound like every other month. Heard through the small speaker of a keypad phone in the mix (narrow band), filter wide enough that consonants survive.

characters.name: अनिल राठौड़ (Anil Rathore), DSP
characters.role: The sub-division's DSP. Holds a press conference at the Imlipur thana at ten tomorrow. Voice only in this episode, on Nandini's phone.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; a man always half addressing the press. City Hindi with a lot of English. Impatient, gives orders as times and places. Phone-filtered in the mix and must stay fully intelligible, above all l17. Never shouts: the last line is level and final.

location: talkies_lobby: the lobby of the shut Roopam Talkies, fitted out as a police station. Terrazzo floor, two round pillars, empty film-poster frames (painted blank). Centre: Nirala's desk, the old booking counter, with registers squared in a stack, the red-cloth thick file, a rubber stamp, a tin ink pad, a kettle and two glasses, and Nirala's small keypad phone lying face up. Behind the desk the hand-painted board (painted blank; overlay ov_fake_board). To one side the complainants' bench, with Nandini's red helmet on it; to the other the ticket-booth lockup with its arched grille window. A wall clock with hands and no numerals. One bare bulb over the desk; the lobby doors open on the dark, and far off through them the red railway signal lamp at the crossing.
time_of_day: Night, about 10:30 p.m. to 11 p.m. One bare bulb; everything outside its circle is dark.

Shot 2 (two-shot across the desk): Nirala in his cap behind the counter, his hands flat either side of the phone; Nandini standing opposite, picture-left. Both are looking down at the phone. l01 plays here. Shot 3 (single): Nandini looks up at him for l02. Silence: 1.5 s of buzzing before l01.

sfx_notes: Bed, whole episode, loopable (one talkies_lobby night ambience for the series): the hum of one bare bulb, crickets outside the open lobby doors, a slow wall-clock tick. Nothing in it is loud.

b1: an old keypad phone on silent-vibrate, rattling hard on a wooden counter; it starts on black, before the first picture, and runs 1.5 s before l01, then stops dead under l01. Shared series effect: make it once.

b2: a soft key click as he presses speaker, then Bhaiyaji through a small phone loudspeaker (narrow band, a little room echo off the terrazzo). Keep the filter wide enough that consonants survive. Bed down under l03 to l06.
b3: after l06, a click and three short end-of-call tones; then only the bulb hum for the 1.2 s hold.
b4: quick footsteps on terrazzo coming in from the dark, the knitting bag's soft thump, Pushpa's breath under l08. The breath dies away before l09.
b5: 1.5 s of near-silence: bulb hum, clock tick, one far dog bark. No music.

b6: the DSP through a phone filter at her ear (narrower than Bhaiyaji's speaker, still intelligible). Nothing loud anywhere in b6: no train, no door. The bed ducks further under l17 so every word of it is clear.
b7: after the last word of l20, and only then, a distant goods-train horn, low and far, fading under b8 shot 1 and l21 (b8 opens on l21; its 1.5 s silence comes after l21).
b8: in the 1.5 s silence, the leather flap unbuttoning and a light hollow knock of wood laid on wood. Not a metallic sound. Nothing else.
b10: in the silence before l27, one dry metallic click of the handcuffs opening; it must be over before the line starts. The bed ducks right down under l27 and stays down through the 1.5 s hold.
music_note: No music for b1 to b5: phone, bulb and crickets only. From b6 a single low sustained string note, barely audible, enters under the DSP call and ducks under l17. It drops out completely for b8 (the revolver is played straight, with no sting). Under b10 one soft sustained note returns, ducked under l27, and is cut to silence at the end of the hold so the question card lands in silence. Instrumental, no melody, no percussion hits.
ending_question: नंदिनी एक डरे हुए, निहत्थे आदमी को lockup में रखकर आठ सौ बोरी SHO की मोहर पर जाने देगी, या अपने ही DSP के order के ख़िलाफ़ उसे उस भैयाजी के पास भेजेगी जिसे शायद पहले से सब पता है?

Where D-016 differs from the bible, D-016 is used: l07 is D-016 direction 1 ('कस्बे का राशन' in place of 'माल के साथ').

Length, counted by hand (no shell in this session, so not by a tool): about 1,025 characters of dialogue, counted as code points with spaces and punctuation, without tags, the space after a tag, or speaker labels, and with nukta letters counted as two code points. Under D-016 direction 7's ceiling of about 1,050 for s2e03. The protected key lines of b4 to b10 alone are about 823 of that. A tool count may differ by a few per cent.

Cuts made to stay inside the measure, given Gate 0b's finding that real v4 takes run 20 to 60 per cent over target: (1) 'त्रिपाठी जी दस हज़ार लेते हैं। आप दो में ख़ुश।' is cut from b2, as D-016 direction 9 allows, because s2e02 b6 keeps 'त्रिपाठी जी से सस्ते भी, मीठे भी।'; 'अकेले आइएगा।' stays. (2) The optional b4 clause on why Pushpa comes late and the optional b5 line 'ना गया, तो वो यहाँ आएँगे, madam।' are not used. (3) b6 joins the DSP call after she has asked for the raid, so she has no opening line; 'raid' is first heard in his refusal (l15), and the beat's action says she has asked. No protected line was cut or reworded beyond the splits below.

Lines split at their sentence breaks, as D-016 direction 8 asks, with a new still between and no added matter: Bhaiyaji's b2 key line (l03, l04, l05, l06), Pushpa's b4 key line (l08, l09), the DSP's b6 key line (l15, l16, l17), Nandini's b7 line 1 (l18, l19), Nirala's b8 line 2 (l22, l23) and his b9 line (l25, l26).

Running time: spoken targets 116.9 s, 13 speaker changes at 0.3 s (3.9 s), silences 12.0 s: 132.8 s, under the 135 s ceiling. The targets assume about 8.8 characters a second, slower than the proof targets, because of the measured Gate 0b overrun. If takes still run long, trim the b10 hold and the b5 and b8 silences before any line; the next line to go would need an entry in the decisions log (D-016).

Silences and where they sit (the proof format has no position key): b1 before l01; b3 before l07; b4 before l08; b5 before l12; b6 before l13; b7 before l18; b8 between l21 and l22 (the revolver is laid down); b9 before l25; b10 1.0 s before l27 and 1.5 s after it.

Names: 'SI जोशी' (l15) is written in Devanagari by the script convention and the beat_outlines note, where the bible's default line has 'SI Joshi'. Nobody says a bare 'साहब': 'DSP साहब', 'SHO साहब', and 'Inspector साहब' only in Bhaiyaji's mouth (l03). Nandini calls Nirala 'ये' and 'यही' two beats before the question (l18, l20), which is why the question says 'इन्हें' (D-006 change 19). Spoken lines use ये and वो only, never the bookish forms.
One word per object: मोहर for the stamp, slip, godown, truck, lockup (Latin), and हथकड़ी only in the question.
l01 'भैयाजी।' is a one-word turn and the bible's key line. Flag it for extra takes; fallback text if it is unstable: 'भैयाजी हैं, madam।'.

Tags: [flatly] on l18 is in the verify group; if the nandini voice ignores it, swap to [calm]. All other tags are from the group used in the proof scenes. No line stacks two tags on one or two words; no tag is followed by an ellipsis; no three whispered lines in a row (no line in this episode is a true whisper). l27, the cliffhanger, is [quietly], meaning low and fully voiced, with the bed ducked under it.
Phone lines: Bhaiyaji (b2) and the DSP (b6) are filtered and never sit on a loud effect; the train horn in b7 comes only after l20 and nowhere near the DSP (bible writer_notes).

Faces per frame (D-016 direction 14): no frame holds more than two sheet faces. b4, b5 and b6 list three on_screen, but the third is hands only (b4 Nirala's sleeves, b5 three sets of hands, b6 Nirala's hands and Pushpa's needles). Pushpa is in the room in b8 to b10 and out of frame.

Props and state (D-013): Nirala's keypad phone face up on the desk from b1; the red-cloth thick file on the desk; Nandini's red helmet on the bench all episode; her own black phone at her right ear in b6, lowered in b7, then in her right trouser pocket to the end, not seen again; Pushpa's keypad handset in its knitted orange cover in her left cardigan pocket all episode, out of sight (the wool is in the right); the wooden revolver holstered on Nirala's right hip until b8, then lying on the desk in profile to the end, never pointed at a face or the camera; the handcuffs in the pouch on her right hip until b10, then open in her right hand; the medal on his chest throughout; the wall clock with no numerals, hands at eleven in b10 (D-016 direction 17).
Stills only (plan section 9): the phone's buzz, the end of the call, Pushpa's walk, the flap unbuttoning and the cuffs opening are carried by sound; each shot shows one visible change.

The ending question is not answered by any spoken line: the last line is the choice itself, and what Bhaiyaji knows is still unknown on screen. Neither the transfer application nor the slip's existing stamp is mentioned (bible balance_rules).
